reviews.title: “A cooler that’s worth it”
reviews.comment:
The media could not be loaded.  https://m.media-amazon.com/images/I/B1Nvl1e4ccL.mp4 https://m.media-amazon.com/images/I/61EkSN9iVQL._SY256.jpg I’m very satisfied with the darkFlash DV360S. Its design is one of its strongest points: the 3.2” LCD display is beautiful, sharp, and fully customizable, perfect for giving my PC a modern and stylish look. The ARGB sync works great, and the PWM fans keep temperatures under control even during gaming or heavy tasks, without being too loud.
Installation was fairly easy, and I appreciate that it’s compatible with so many Intel and AMD sockets. The software to control the screen could be more stable, and some people might have issues with the USB not being recognized, but in my case everything worked properly.
Overall, it delivers what it promises: good cooling performance, great aesthetics, and excellent value for the price. If you’re looking for a 360mm AIO that cools well and looks amazing inside your case, this model is a very solid choice. ✔️

reviews.title: AM4 Compatible, despite negative reviews saying otherwise
reviews.comment:
IF YOU HAVE AN AM4, READ THIS BEFORE PURCHASING!
I saw a few people complaining in the reviews about how this cooler doesn’t fit am4 motherboards. They’re both right and wrong. I have an AM4, and was unable to mount the cooler on my old AM4 mounting bracket. AM4 cooler mounting brackets have changed over the years, and only the current model works/fits with the cooler.
You can easily find an AM4 CPU bracket for less than $10 on Amazon. They’re super easy to install, and once I installed a newer bracket, the CPU cooler fit just fine.
Aside from the initial instillation hiccup (due to my older model of CPU cooler mounting bracket), this CPU cooler works great. My only complaint is that the mounting bracket doesn’t come with the cooler. Most CPU coolers come with that bracket. Not a huge deal, but definitely something to keep in mind.

reviews.title: Cooler died in about a year!
reviews.comment: This cooler was a great cooler in the beginning, but you do get what you pay for. I noticed the temps climbing in VR operations and didn't understand why my computer was shutting down until i noticed the operating temps. I checked the cooler and it was empty! no coolant in the system, it all leaked out. The main take away is that most AIO coolers will fail, sadly this cooler dried up in about a year.
